commands.command: Decision 0051: explicit ROG capability, brownfield bootstrap, backfill, and clean-clone contract
commands.summary: Defines the five-state capability model (LegacyAbsent/LegacyEnabled/ExplicitDisabled/ExplicitEnabled/EnabledMissing), the narrow committed capability declaration (governance/rog-capability.json, schema-validated, outside rog/), enable-after-proof-good ordering, explicit disable semantics, adoption opt-in (--graph), backfill-is-not-automatic (no doctor auto-enable), the .gitignore enablement guard, and read-only-query-never-mutates-capability.

228/228 (199 pre-existing at checkpoint start + 29 new: 7 capability unit tests, 9 status.rs ROG-039 state-matrix tests, 6 lifecycle tests in lib.rs, 1 EnabledButMissing query-open test, 6 real-git-clone tests in the new clean_clone_tests.rs).

Full workspace green on Windows and, independently, on Linux-native WSL2 Debian (~/repopact-linux, synced to this checkpoint's exact pushed commit, never /mnt/c/...): identical 228 repopact-graph tests and 16 repopact-repository tests pass on both platforms.
Clean on every commit in this checkpoint.

repopact/schemas/rog-capability.schema.json (draft 2020-12), {"$schema":"../repopact/schemas/rog-capability.schema.json","version":1,"capabilities":{"rog":"enabled"|"disabled"}}. Excluded from the source projection fingerprint (projection.rs::is_capability_declaration) for the same self-referential-churn reason rog/ itself is excluded. Never indexed as a graph node or given a RecordKind variant, avoiding a closed-enum-in-durable-graph hazard, and deliberately not a general settings system.

CapabilityState::{LegacyAbsent,LegacyEnabled,ExplicitDisabled,ExplicitEnabled,EnabledMissing} computed purely as a function of (declaration on disk, rog/manifest.json existence), orthogonal to Freshness/GraphCoverageState. Threaded through GraphStatus.capability_state, GraphQueryContext.capability_state, SessionGraphState::query_context, and the desktop-api call site. All 8 required ROG-039 states proven by dedicated tests in status.rs; EnabledMissing never flattens to Absent anywhere in the query-open path (query::open::QueryOpenError::EnabledButMissing is a distinct variant, checked before the freshness match, fails closed even with allow_stale).

durable::write() -- the single choke point used by full build, full-rebuild fallback, and incremental update -- calls capability::persist_enabled() only after swap_with_rollback has already succeeded. A build that fails never leaves capability falsely enabled (proven by build_persists_explicit_enabled_capability and by the adoption bootstrap-failure test).

commands.command: Explicit disable (repopact graph disable, Decision 0051 section 4)
commands.summary: durable::disable() removes rog/ (if present) then persists capabilities.rog=disabled; idempotent; never touches source/governance/lifecycle records outside rog/. CLI subcommand added (repopact/graph_cli.py). Test sequence enabled->disable->validate->status->build->enabled proven (build_disable_rebuild_re_enables, disable_is_idempotent, plus 3 CLI-level pytest tests including test_build_disable_rebuild_cycle_via_cli).

test_read_only_commands_never_enable_capability (Python CLI) plus the Rust query-path tests prove graph.status/verify/resolve/orient/dependencies/tests/governance have zero enablement side effect; a query failure never rewrites capability state.

doctor.py::_rog_capability_drift reports (fixable=False, no corresponding fix() action) graph.capability-malformed / enabled-but-missing / stale-or-corrupt-or-unsupported-while-enabled and recommends `repopact graph build`, but never silently enables or rebuilds. Proven by test_doctor_never_auto_enables_rog_on_a_legacy_absent_repo and test_doctor_reports_enabled_but_missing_and_never_repairs_it.

durable::check_enablement_not_ignored issues one bounded `git check-ignore -- rog/` invocation (trailing slash required -- a bare 'rog' pathspec is ambiguous against a directory-anchored .gitignore pattern and was confirmed, by direct manual reproduction, to falsely report 'not ignored'). Checked before enablement is ever reported successful; never rewrites the user's .gitignore. Proven by ignored_durable_graph_refuses_to_report_enablement_success and a_gitignored_rog_directory_never_survives_to_a_clone.

Default `repopact adopt` remains graph-off (backward compatible; test_adopt_default_leaves_graph_off). `--graph` runs discovery -> governance adoption -> governance validation -> _run_graph_bootstrap (graph.build -> graph.verify -> graph.orient against the adoption work item, via EngineClient only -- no python_graph_builder, no duplicated query kernel). Report gains graph_requested/graph_capability/graph_build/graph_verify/orientation_summary/graph_error, preserving existing report compatibility (test_adopt_graph_orchestrates_discovery_through_orientation). --dry-run --graph writes nothing graph-related (test_adopt_dry_run_graph_writes_nothing_graph_related, confirmed against a real disposable repo below). A monkeypatched EngineClient raising EngineUnavailableError proves a bootstrap failure never fabricates or rolls back governance and makes the CLI exit non-zero only when --graph was explicitly requested (test_adopt_graph_bootstrap_failure_does_not_fabricate_or_rollback_governance); governance is left standing (not rolled back) -- a deliberate choice, documented here: hiding a valid governance adoption to mask an unrelated graph failure would itself be a correctness violation.

commands.command: ROG-016: real git-clone proof (rust/crates/repopact-graph/src/clean_clone_tests.rs, new file)
commands.summary: 6 tests using actual `git init`/`add`/`commit`/`clone` subprocesses (never a directory copy), skipping (not failing) when git is unavailable: (1) clean_clone_carries_capability_and_durable_graph_byte_identical -- capability declaration, manifest, and every node shard are byte-identical between source and clone; (2) clean_clone_validates_and_reports_fresh_without_a_rebuild -- status() on the fresh clone reports ExplicitEnabled+Fresh with zero diagnostics, no graph.build call anywhere in the test; (3) clean_clone_answers_bounded_queries_from_the_committed_graph -- resolve/orient/dependencies/tests all answer from the committed graph, never rebuilt; (4) clean_clone_queries_invoke_no_additional_git -- CountingGitRunner proves zero additional Git invocations on the query path after clone; (5) damaged_clone_with_rog_removed_is_a_hard_failure_not_absent -- deliberately removing rog/ from an enabled clone reports capability=enabled+graph=missing+validation failure, never 'graph absent, repository valid', directly proving the ROG-039 missing-state distinction; (6) a_gitignored_rog_directory_never_survives_to_a_clone -- an ignored rog/ refuses enablement success without modifying .gitignore.

commands.command: ROG-016: discovered and fixed a real product defect -- Windows Git core.autocrlf corruption on clone
commands.summary: This machine's Git-for-Windows has core.autocrlf=true at the SYSTEM config level (confirmed via `git config --system --get core.autocrlf`, overriding false at user/repo scope), which silently rewrites LF to CRLF on checkout. This corrupted the durable graph's SHA-256 hashes on clone (reported Corrupt), and after a first narrow .gitattributes fix limited to rog/, was still mangling ordinary source files enough to shift the whole source-projection fingerprint (reported Stale instead of Fresh). Per this checkpoint's explicit directive, treated as a real defect, not normalized away. Fixed with a repo-wide .gitattributes protection (`* -text` plus explicit rog/** and governance/rog-capability.json entries) written non-destructively by durable::ensure_gitattributes_protects_durable_graph() at the start of build_and_write(), before the fingerprint is computed. Verified via manual git init/gitattributes/add/commit/clone/xxd byte reproduction that this resolves both the Corrupt and Stale symptoms; all 6 clean_clone_tests then passed. Four pre-existing hundred-file-fixture tests with hardcoded exact file/reuse counts needed a documented +1 adjustment because .gitattributes became new legitimate tracked content.

commands.command: ROG-016: discovered and fixed a second real defect -- a linked worktree's own .git pointer file leaking into the source projection
commands.summary: While proving the RepoPact-scale backfill (below) using a disposable `git worktree` copy, a build inside the worktree produced a graph one node/two edges larger than an identical build in a plain clone of the same commit, and the plain clone (correctly) reported the worktree-built graph Stale after being re-cloned. Root cause: rust/crates/repopact-repository/src/lib.rs's walk_files_inner applied the IGNORED_PARTS ('.git' among them) exclusion only to directory entries, never to plain files -- and a linked worktree's own `.git` is a plain pointer file (e.g. 'gitdir: /path/.git/worktrees/name'), never a directory, so it slipped through and was indexed as an ordinary file:.git graph node. Fixed by applying the same ignored-name check to file entries. Added a_worktree_roots_own_git_pointer_file_is_excluded_from_files_under as a regression test. This defect is orthogonal to the autocrlf issue and specific to running `graph build` inside a linked worktree; it does not affect an ordinary clone (the primary ROG-016 clean-clone path), which was independently proven correct before this defect was found.
